findings.title: TERMINAL_FRAME lane omits the Node-status and tenant-execution conditions of actual terminal._current
findings.source: lifecycle.py:318-332 _terminal_parent_current; register :64-67; invoke :90-95 (no n['liveness'] / projection check). Actual 72028 terminal.py:65 require_execution (tenant kill_switch), :76-84 node status in {online,draining} and recovery_epoch; frame() calls _current at terminal.py:229 then snapshot(observation_only=True) at :275, which itself skips status/heartbeat.
findings.counterexample: PLAIN and B: register EXECUTE parent, invoke; set Node liveness offline (what actual NodeObservation.mark_offline does; it never releases leases). TERMINAL_FRAME register -> handle, invoke -> True; prepared-then-offline invoke -> True. The model's own R12 eligible() query returns False for the same frame. Same result on immutable Rev7 and Rev8 models (reviewer-offline-frame-probe-result.jsonl.txt).
findings.impact: The proposed guard is weaker than the installed product guard on the exact condition the T1 demonstrator writes; adopting it as the contract would let a terminal frame reach a Node the CP has declared lost. No tenant execution-stop (kill switch) condition is modelled for the frame lane either.
findings.remedy: In register/invoke/confirm for TERMINAL_FRAME require projection(n) in {online, draining} (draining == DRAIN fact, matching actual status enum) and a modelled tenant execution containment equal to actual require_execution; add PLAIN+B regressions (offline before register, offline after prepare, draining positive, tenant stop refuses) and keep cleanup read / CANCEL / RECEIPT lanes unchanged.
